name: Power Grid Corporation of India Limited

items.statement: FY26 capex revised to Rs 35,000+ crore, already achieved; capitalization revised to Rs 25,000+ crore
items.quote: I am happy to announce that last investors meet, we have revised our Capex guideline to Rs. 32,000 crore. So today, we are now announcing that our Capex guideline will be Rs. 35,000 plus crore, and already we have achieved Rs. 35,000 crore.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance Rs 45,000 crore; capitalization Rs 30,000 crore; FY28 capitalization Rs 35,000 crore
items.quote: For next financial year, it will be Rs. 45,000 crore Capex. Similarly capitalisation. This year, Rs. 25,000 crore next year, Rs. 30,000 crore, then in FY28 it is going to be Rs. 35,000 crore.

items.statement: Works in hand Rs 1.48 lakh crore including CWIP of Rs 49,000 crore; Leh-Pang Kaithal excluded
items.value: 148000 crore works in hand; 49000 crore CWIP
items.quote: We have works in hand about Rs. 1,48,000 crores, and CWIP is about more than Rs. 49,000 crores.

items.statement: Multi-year transmission opportunity visibility Rs 15 lakh crore including Rs 7.9 lakh crore national, Rs 3-4 lakh crore international, Rs 4 lakh crore Brahmaputra basin
items.quote: So total, the visibility for transmission project is will be somewhere Rs. 15 lakh crore, investment in transmission system, considering national international inter-state, inter-state, all projects will be somewhere about Rs. 15 lakh crore.

items.statement: Average annual capex requirement Rs 60,000-70,000 crore for next 10 years; equity requirement Rs 12,000-14,000 crore per year
items.quote: So, considering, even if we have, say, Rs. 70,000 crores means equity will be, say, 20%. So, 16 to 20 somewhere we will have about Rs. 12,000 crore requirements of equity.

items.statement: FY26 transmission availability 99.84%; trippings 0.25 per line; 4,239 ckm lines and ~62,000 MVA transformation capacity commissioned
items.quote: This financial year, we are having availability of 99.84%. Trippings per line, 0.25 trippings per line, that means our one line trips in every 4 years on an average.

items.statement: Execution capacity scaled from Rs 8,000-9,000 crore to Rs 35,000 crore in 3 years; developing more vendors and trained manpower
items.quote: In last 3 to 4 years, we have been doing capex of about Rs. 8,000 to 9,000 crores. Last to last year, we did Rs. 12,500 crores. Last year, we did Rs. 26,000 crores. This year, we have done Rs. 35,000 crores.

items.statement: RoW compensation guidelines revised: 30% rural, 45% semi-urban, 60% urban/metro at market rate; dedicated RoW cells established
items.quote: RoW issue has been addressed by Government of India by announcing the revised guidelines for compensation for land diminution value, they have increased to 30% for rural area, 45% of semi-urban area, 60% for urban area, metro cities.

items.statement: 7 skill development centers to train 1,400-1,500 technicians annually; 100+ erection gangs per year
items.quote: Now, we have already 5 skilled developmental centers in which we are training about 50 fitters or technicians in 3 months and now 2 more are coming, so we will have almost 7 skill development centers.

items.statement: Transformer/reactor manufacturer capacity augmentation to >4 lakh MVA/year, exceeding demand
items.quote: Similarly, for transformers and reactors supply and other equipment supply, all manufacturers are now going for augmentation of their capacity. The augmentation capacity will be mo re than 4 lakh MVA capacity each year

items.statement: MCA approval received for merging 19 SPVs into 2; Board approved merging 28 wholly-owned subsidiaries into 2; seeking DIPAM limit increase to Rs 10,000-15,000 crore
items.quote: Recently, with the support of Government of India, we have now approval for merging 19 SPVs into 2 SPVs, MCA approval has been received. Now we are also considering merger of 28 Whol ly owned subsidiaries into 2 wholly owned subsidiaries

items.statement: SPV mergers require CERC, DIPAM, MCA approvals; focus on administrative control not cost savings
items.quote: For any merger, we used to take the approval of the regulators. Yeah, last time also, when we merged 19 companies into two, we took the approval of the regulator in addition to DIPAM.

items.statement: Peak demand expected 270-275 GW in May-June 2025; grid prepared to meet requirement per Minister review
items.quote: We are going to have almost 270 GW requirement in May or June, and for which we have sufficient resources to meet that requirement.

items.statement: CEA 2035 plan: 786 GW non-fossil capacity, 1100 GW total capacity, 459 GW peak demand by 2035-36
items.quote: per 2035 CEA guideline, it says that by 2035 - Power Grid Corporation of 36, we will have 786 GW renewable capacity, and total capacity will be somewhere about 1100 GW

items.statement: TBCB win rate >50% historically; intend to maintain 50% win rate; not aggressive in intrastate small projects
items.quote: Already, whatever projects we have won under TBCB, our winning percentage has been more than 50%, till today. So, we would like to maintain that 50%.

items.statement: TBCB projects: land compensation escalation passed through via CERC tariff; force majeure conditions compensated
items.quote: There has been some price escalation considering this compensation towards land diminution value. And in case such force majure conditions are there, we are claiming extra tariff from CERC, which is normally given approved by CERC.

items.statement: GIB court ruling no impact on POWERGRID projects; all projects outside GIB area; CTUIL ensuring future projects avoid GIB areas
items.quote: So, we don't have any impact of GIB in Rajasthan or Ramga rh, that area. So, our projects were… whatever projects, transmission projects were there, it is outside that area

items.statement: New AC project timelines 30-36 months; 18-24 month timelines not feasible given RoW and supply chain
items.quote: We have, based on our experience, we have given feedback to Government of India that, 18 months or 24 months is not feasible. This timeline is not right. So, at least we should get 30 months or 36 months.

items.statement: Participating in BESS but not winning; seeking battery supplier tie-ups to optimize cost; BESS at generation end to increase transmission utilization
items.quote: Regarding the battery energy storage, we are participating, but we are not able to win, best projects, because in competition there are a number of small, smaller players. And, we have one, only one project.

items.statement: Paid >Rs 50,000 crore dividends FY21-26; dividend yield 3-4%; market cap 2.5x growth FY21-26
items.quote: In last 5 years from FY 21 to FY 26, we have paid dividends more than Rs. 50,000 crores to our investors, to our shareholders. And on last February 2026 our market Capitalization was Rs. 2,77,000 crore.

items.statement: Profit Rs 15,000+ crore currently, expected Rs 17,000-20,000 crore; sufficient internal accruals to fund equity portion of capex without external raise
items.quote: So today we have profit of Rs. 15,000 plus and as we go ahead, this profit will go to, say, Rs. 17,000, 18,000, 20,000. So, even considering our, compulsory dividend payout, which is about Rs. 5000 crores.

items.statement: HVDC interconnections planned with Sri Lanka, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Singapore, Maldives, Myanmar; Rs 3-4 lakh crore visibility
items.quote: If we consider HVDC, interconnections with Sri Lanka, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Singapore, Maldives, and Myanmar, then another Rs. 3 lakh crore to 4 lakh crore, visibility is there.

items.statement: Expect over 40% growth across key parameters in FY27 as new expansion stabilizes over 3-4 months
items.quote: Accordingly, we expect to deliver growth of over 40% across key parameters during the current year.

items.statement: Expect revenue increase of around Rs. 500 crore in FY27 taking total to Rs. 2,900-3,000 crore based on 165,000 tons capacity increase at Rs. 60,000 per ton
items.value: Rs. 500 crore increase to Rs. 2,900-3,000 crore
items.quote: 165,000 tons is the capacity increase, 40 -50% also, if you consider it, 80,000 tons into around Rs. 60,000 per ton. So, you can expect a top line increase of around Rs. 500 crore. So, this year we had around Rs. 2,400 odd crore. So, you expect an increase of around Rs. 500 crore more, Rs. 2,900 to Rs. 3,000.

items.statement: Expect 35-40% revenue growth in FY27 including import and manufacturing
items.quote: Yes, including the import and manufacturing we expect 40% growth should not be a big issue.

items.statement: Expect to import around 150,000 metric tons translating to approximately Rs. 1,000 crore revenue in FY27; manufacturing growth around 25%
items.quote: For FY27, based on market demand, we expect to import around 150,000 metric tons of material, which would translate into approxi mately Rs.1,000 crore of revenue . And based on the capacity utilization on a reasonable level, the growth in the manufacturing will be in the range of 25

items.statement: Margins under pressure in FY27; FY26 levels may not be fully sustainable; some moderation expected as portion of raw material cost increases absorbed by company, some by government, some passed to farmers
items.quote: As mentioned earlier, margins will be under pressure, and the levels achieved in FY26 may not be fully sustainable. There will be some moderation, as a portion of the increase in raw material costs will be absorbed by the company, some by the Government of India, and some will be passed on to farmers.

items.statement: Difficult to quantify margin impact currently; working on sourcing raw materials at reasonable prices; price increases to be passed to customers; no significant long-term impact expected but some pressure in Q1
items.quote: At present, it is difficult to quantify, as we are still working on sourcing raw mater ials at reasonable prices and that reasonable price increase will be passed on to the customers because subsidy has already been announced. So, we do not expect a significant long -term impact; however, there may be some pressure in the first quarter

items.statement: EBITDA per ton on manufacturing side maintained at FY25 levels around Rs. 5,200-5,500 per ton in FY26
items.quote: The EBITDA for FY25 has largely been maintained in FY26.

items.statement: Trading business EBITDA margin around 5-6%; net margin after interest and depreciation around 2.5-3%
items.quote: EBITDA margin is 5% to 6% in in trading business.

items.statement: No additional capex or expansion plans beyond completed expansion; whatever planned has been implemented
items.quote: No, so far, we have not planned anything. Whatever we have, it has been implemented.

items.statement: Maintenance capex and future expansion plans not disclosed; will declare once finalized and approved by regulators
items.quote: See, when we have not declared with the regulators, we cannot come out right now. It is on part of the statutory obligation to declare with the regulator and then only we can come out with the exact CAPEX for the year.

items.statement: NPK/DAP capacity enhanced by 50% to 495,000 MTPA; SSP capacity 120,000 MTPA; total phosphatic fertilizer capacity 615,000 MTPA; sulphuric acid capacity 99,000 MTPA
items.quote: NPK/DAP capacity enhanced by 50% to 495,000 MTPA and existing SSP capacity at 120,000 MTPA, taking total phosphatic fertilizer capacity to 615,000 MTPA. Backward integration strengthened with sulphuric acid capacity of 99,000 MTPA.

items.statement: New expansion commenced production in April; expect stabilization over 3-4 months; full utilization in subsequent quarters
items.quote: The new expansion has commenced this month, and there may be some initial teething issues in the first or second quarter. However, we expect this capacity to be fully utilized in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Plants operating above 100% capacity in FY26 reflecting strong demand and efficient operations
items.quote: Maintained healthy utilization across NPK/DAP and SSP plants, with certain units operating above 100% capacity, reflecting strong demand and efficient plant operations

items.statement: Fertilizer production 94,103 MT in Q4 FY26; total production 397,263 MT in FY26
items.quote: Achieved total production of 397,263 MT, supported by High demand across markets

items.statement: Input costs increased from mid-February due to supply constraints, tight gas-linked production, higher logistics and freight; ammonia and sulphur prices firmed up
items.quote: from mid -February onwards, global market witness ed firming trends driven by supply-side constraints, tightness in gas-linked production, higher logistic and freight costs. As a result, ammonia prices moved up sequentially during the quarter. Sulphur prices also firmed up towards March.

items.statement: Sulphur prices currently in range of Rs. 55,000-70,000 per ton depending on supplier, timing and payment terms; prices changed significantly in last 30-45 days
items.quote: The prices are changing and prices are in the range of around Rs.55,000 to Rs.70,000 per ton, depending on the supplier and what time we are buying and what are the payment terms. It is changing. It has changed a lot in the last 30 days, 45 days, and we are expecting changes in another 30 days.

items.statement: MRP increases initiated to pass on cost increases; NBS subsidy announced for next six months; balance impact to be passed to consumers
items.quote: The government has already announced the NBS policy, and we have initiated steps to revise MRPs accordingly.

items.statement: Shift towards NPK complexes and SSPs due to DAP prices and availability; integrated players with diversified portfolios better positioned
items.quote: DAP prices and availability have led to gradual shifts towards more cost-effective and balanced nutrient solutions, including NPK complexes and SSPs.

items.statement: Manufacturing only one NPK variant (20-20-0-13); importing other variants to meet market demand and provide full product range
items.quote: We have b een producing one variant at 20-20-0-13 and even the demand of this product, we have not been able to meet adequately. As a result, our plants are operating purely on this one product. Now, to meet the market demand and just that our consumers should think that we are capable of providing all variants, we import other variants and that we supply

items.statement: Receivables increased due to imported NPK variants supplied in last quarter; subsidy receivables normally 50-55 days; expect realization in current quarter
items.quote: As a result, on the balance sheet side, on the day, March end closing, the receivable levels are going up. But for subsidy, our receivable levels are normally in the range of 50-55 days.

items.statement: Subsidy receivable ~Rs. 400 crore; other receivables Rs. 300-325 crore; expect realization in current quarter; no cash flow stress foreseen
items.quote: subsidy receivable is almost Rs.400 crore and other receivables are in the range of Rs.300 crore to Rs.325 crore. Praveen Ostwal: We expect these amounts to be realized during the current quarter. Accordingly, we do not foresee any stress on the cash flow position

items.statement: Raw material inventory increased from ~Rs. 60 crore to Rs. 93 crore; supplies to cooperatives pending invoicing due to inspection formalities
items.quote: Raw material inventory increased from approximately Rs.60 crore to Rs.93 crore. Additionally, the apparent increase is largely due to supplies made to cooperative institutions. In such cases, invoices cannot be raised until inspection and related formalities are completed.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded by CRISIL to A+ (Stable); negative outlook applies to industry not company
items.quote: We are also pleased to highlight that our credit rating has been upgraded by CRISIL to A+ (Stable), reflecting improved financial strength and business fundamentals

items.statement: Effective interest cost on working capital borrowings in range of 6% to 7.5%; foreign currency borrowings cost relatively lower
items.quote: Overall, the effective interest cost is in the range of 6% to 7.5%.

items.statement: No procurement issues for sulphur; only price impact being managed; plants fully operational
items.quote: There are no issues in procurement. The only impact is from the increase in prices, which we are actively managing to secure the best possible rates. Ultimately, the cost increases will have to be passed on to consumers. Our plants are fully operational.

items.statement: Green ammonia supply expected after approximately 3 years; currently relying on grey ammonia; gas supply to urea manufacturers restored to 100% easing ammonia availability
items.quote: As for green ammonia, it is expected to be available only after approximately three years. In the interim, we will continue to rely on grey ammonia. Recent developments indicate that gas supply to urea manufacturers has been restored to 100%, which should ease ammonia availability over the next week.

items.statement: Beneficiation capacity ~200,000 tons; current utilization 50-75%; produced >70,000 MT high-grade rock phosphate last year; conversion ratio ~2-2.5 tons low-grade rock per ton output (indicative)
items.quote: For reference, last year, against a beneficiation capacity of 200,000 tons, we produced more than 70,000 metric tons of high-grade rock phosphate. Praveen Ostwal: Broadly, if the input grade is around 15% and the output is around 30%, approximately 2 to 2.5 tons of low-grade rock may be required

items.statement: Domestic fertilizer demand expected to remain stable; monsoon forecast ~95% of normal not a major variation; reservoir water levels higher; food demand non-negotiable
items.quote: The monsoon f orecast is around 95% of normal, which is not a major variation. Also, water levels in major reservoirs, rivers, and borewells are higher compared to earlier periods in the country. Therefore, we do not expect any stress on the agriculture sector, and cons equently, fertilizer demand is expected to remain

items.statement: Domestic manufacturers insulated from demand pressure as ~40% of phosphatic fertilizers are imported; any softening absorbed by imports first
items.quote: Even hypothetically, if demand were to soften, it is important to note that nearly 40% of phosphatic fertilizers are imported. Therefore, any impact would first be absorbed by imports, and domestic manufacturers would remain relatively insulated.

items.statement: Subsidy forms ~40% of revenue for NPK; recent subsidy announcement does not fully compensate input cost increase; shortfall to be addressed through MRP adjustments
items.quote: For NPK, approximately 40% of revenue is derived from subsidy support. While the recent subsidy announcement does not fully compensate for the increase in input costs, the shortfall will be addressed through MRP adjustments.

items.statement: Targets 30-35% top-line growth next financial year
items.quote: And we still… we see that, okay, at least we would do around a 30 -35% growth from… compared to this year. is what we are looking to do for the next financial year.

items.statement: Plans Rs 2-3 crore capex in Q1 next year from internal accruals
items.quote: Maybe a CAPEX of another 2 -3 crores would be required, but that we can… we can… Manage that.

items.statement: Current utilisation around 75%; sees 20-25% headroom
items.quote: See, currently, I would say we are utilizing around 75% of our capacity. There is potential to utilize around 20-25% more capacity.

items.statement: After Rs 2-3 crore capex, revenue capacity seen at Rs 140-150 crore
items.quote: After another 2-3 crores of capex that we are looking to do, I think we should be able to go up to around 140, 150, within the range of 140, 150 as a top line.

items.statement: Entered furniture lighting with Hettich vendor approval; developing facade and GaN power supplies
items.quote: We have started working with Hettich, which is into furniture lighting, and we have been onboarded as a vendor, by Hettich. For furniture lighting.

items.statement: GaN power supply models developed; in client talks for launch
items.quote: we've successfully developed all models, and we are at the current phase where we have… we're in talks with our clients to launch all these products in the market

items.statement: Client onboarding typically takes 6-8 months
items.quote: So, general time to acquire a client is generally 6-8 months.

items.statement: Hettich vendor approval covers global supplies; may need dedicated factory
items.quote: the kind of vendor approval that we have got is not only for Indian supplies, it is for global supplies.

items.statement: Passes raw-material price changes to customers beyond a threshold
items.quote: whenever such things happen, the prices increase, we pass on those price increases to our customers, and it's there in the entire chain.

items.statement: Working to reduce inventory days; peaks at Diwali and post-Chinese New Year
items.quote: we are already working on reducing our inventory days. So generally what happens, the two times that we have to publish our numbers, one is in the March and one is September, those are the times specifically where our inventories are higher.

items.statement: Aims to reduce borrowings as inventory liquidates and capex completes
items.quote: as we liquidate more of our… some of our inventory, we'll obviously… the idea would be to reduce the borrowings.

items.statement: Application-based lighting (furniture, facade) targeted for higher margins
items.quote: When you get into application -based lighting, like furniture lighting, or facade lighting, or automobile lighting, or mining lights, or underwater lights. These are products with specific applications, and you're solving a specific problem, so there are margins which are better in this particular

items.statement: Strategy focuses on blue-ocean niches with limited competition
items.quote: We've always tried… our strategy has always been to work in the blue ocean, and not in the red ocean. Blue ocean being where there's not much competition.

items.statement: BIS certification for new lighting models no longer granted to Chinese manufacturers
items.quote: Now, what the government has done is that they have the BIS certification, which was being given to the Chinese manufacturers earlier. Now, no new Chinese manufacturers are being given the BIS certification.

items.statement: Exploring BESS (Battery Energy Storage Systems); early stage, targeting assembly/manufacturing in 2-3 years
items.quote: we intend to get into assembly or manufacturing in future. That could be 2 years down the line, that could be 3 years down the line.

items.statement: BESS opportunity estimated at 30-50 MW annually (~Rs 30-50 crore) if executed
items.quote: We are intending to do… At, if nothing much, at least some 30 to 50 megawatt. What item? So that would roughly convert to around 30 to 50 crores per annum

items.statement: Mainboard migration eligible by September; preparation underway
items.quote: We would be eligible… in September, because I think there's a 3 -year clause, so by September, we will be eligible, and we are much in preparation of how and when we can… how soon can we migrate to the main board.

items.statement: Strengthened team with senior hires across development, operations, sales
items.quote: We have recruited better people in our team. We have got senior people in our team, from development to operations to sales

items.statement: Dollar and crude price volatility affects import costs; passed on after threshold
items.quote: you see that the dollar prices… the dollar has gone up. It affects our imports, the crude has gone up, so it affects the materials that we buy.

items.statement: Exports currently indirect via clients to Middle East, Africa, SAFTA region
items.quote: Currently, we're exporting, but not directly. Our clients are buying from us, and they are exporting to other countries. They're exporting to the Middle East, they've been exporting to Africa, they've been exporting to the Safda region.

items.statement: Lighting demand seasonal: stronger June-March, softer in Q1 and year-end
items.quote: Currently, because we're predominantly catering to the Indian market, So, it becomes a little of a cyclic business also at times, because the lighting requirement kind of shoots up from June, July. And goes on till… till March.

items.statement: Prices adjusted only when raw-material moves beyond a threshold band
items.quote: Definitely, that happens only after a certain threshold limit. We know that the price escalation has gone up beyond a certain percentage. Kundan Edifice Limited 25 March 2026 that is when we can, you know, increase the prices for our customers

items.statement: Industry 4.0 automation (SAP, HRMS, PMS) underway to reduce labour dependence
items.quote: we're working on implementation of software like SAP, We are doing HRMS software, PMS software, we are trying to integrate, we're trying to work on the Industry 4.0.

items.statement: Management aims to grow non-ADHO portfolio to INR500 crores over next three years
items.quote: we will be further focusing on growing this portfolio to around INR500 crores in size over the next three years.

items.statement: Full year gross margin improved 650 bps to 60%
items.quote: we have delivered a gross margin of 60% and a full year EBITDA of INR224 crores at a margin of 19.5%

items.statement: Q4 standalone gross margin at 63%, EBITDA margin at 25%
items.quote: our gross margin stood at 63% for the quarter and 60% for the full year, registering a significant improvement of around 650 basis points against the last year on a full year basis.

items.statement: Management aspires to operate EBITDA margins in low to mid 20s range
items.quote: We said that anywhere from low 20s to mid 20s is where we would aspire to operate and that is where we continue to aspire.

items.statement: ADHO delivered full year revenue growth in 20s with near double-digit volume growth on adjusted ml basis in Q4
items.quote: ADHO has delivered a stupendous year with a full year revenue growth in the 20s. What gives us great joy is that while this growth came across pack groups and channels.

items.statement: General trade grew high teens for full year; urban outperformed rural
items.quote: In the current quarter, we saw a continued recovery in our general trade channel, which grew ahead of the other channels and has delivered a strong teens growth on a full year basis.

items.statement: Organized trade grew 20s YoY in Q4 and now contributes 30% of overall sales
items.quote: Organized trade as a channel continued to perform well. It registered a strong 20s growth Y-o-Y in quarter 4. And within organized trade, modern trade and e-commerce performed well and ahead of the channel.

items.statement: Non-ADHO portfolio reached INR225 crores in FY26 and is profitable
items.quote: we have delivered a revenue of INR225 crores from the non-ADHO portfolio, which we internally refer to as growth portfolio. This portfolio is already a positive contribution portfolio and a profitable portfolio for us.

items.statement: Banjara's grew double-digit in first year under Bajaj ownership with low-teen margins
items.quote: Banjara’s, which was in its bajaj co first year under Bajaj ownership, saw a double-digit growth for the year and a low-teen margin delivery

items.statement: Input cost inflation across nearly 100% of cost base; LLP and packaging volatile due to Gulf war
items.quote: nearly 100% of our cost base is under inflation. It is just that some of them is under maybe a 50%, 60% inflation and some is under that 20%, 30% inflation.

items.statement: MLH reductions taken in Q4; frontal pricing planned for current quarter to manage inflation
items.quote: in the gone quarter, quarter 4, we've already taken certain MLH adjustments, which we have mentioned about, which also basically help in terms of margin for us. And in this quarter, I think we will have to take some amount of frontal pricing as well to manage the quarter.

items.statement: Project Aarohan phase 3 starting in five new states in FY27
items.quote: we are getting into the third phase of Aarohan which involves us going to five new states where we had not gone so far. And we would be executing our entire playbook of Aarohan in these states.

items.statement: Aarohan delivers 2-3% growth delta in implemented areas; covers two-thirds of business currently
items.quote: what we've experienced is around anywhere given to 2% to 3% improvement, delta performance for us in places where we have done Aarohan versus places where we have not done Aarohan.

items.statement: Vishal Personal Care acquired in Q1 FY26; first year in consolidated revenues
items.quote: we've acquired a company in quarter 1 of this year called Vishal Personal Care, which is seeing its first year into the consolidated revenues.

items.statement: Advertising spends up 34% YoY in Q4; maintained at ~15% of revenue for FY26
items.quote: Our consolidated advertising spends for the quarter were up 34% against the same period last year. We are very happy with the SOV intensity being maintained by us

items.statement: International business declined overall; Nepal and Bangladesh grew with Bangladesh breakeven
items.quote: In international business, we overall had a challenging year. This business declined in this quarter. In the key markets of Nepal and Bangladesh, however, we saw growth and the highlight for us in this channel was the breakeven of Bangladesh and further ma rgin improvement in Nepal

items.statement: Leadership change in international business; new leadership focusing on Rest of World and MENA turnaround
items.quote: At an overall basis, in IB, we also had a leadership change. And with the new leadership, we have renewed our efforts behind getting and fixing the markets of Rest of World and MENA

items.statement: Hyperinflation in input costs may require further pricing and cost actions beyond Q1
items.quote: If the hyperinflation continues as it is continuing right now, we will have to further fine-tune our actions going quarter 2 onwards to see how we will continue to protect our margins and be fair to the consumers at the same time.

items.statement: Company holds <10% market share in hair oil category; significant headroom for share gains
items.quote: we have a less than 10% market share in our category. So a less than 10% category player basically shouldn't worry about too many things. We just have to execute and win our space and gain more share in our category.

items.statement: Hair oil category not a sunset sector; $2B+ market with 92% penetration growing at high single digits
items.quote: I don't believe hair oil is a sunset sector. It's a $2 billion plus market with a 20% plus margin with a 92% penetration. There are not too many categories in the country which have 90% penetration, have basically such large bases, continue to operate profitably and grow at a high single digit year-on-year.

items.statement: Management declined to provide MRR guidance for FY27, citing rapid weekly changes and preferring quarter-on-quarter tracking
items.quote: We want to be very, very growth-focused. That being said, I think it would not do justice to do a MRR guidance for one year in the future. The future is changing very, very rapidly week on week.

items.statement: Cluster 1 B200 1024 GPUs expected to go live by mid-May, with another 1024 planned in a couple of months
items.quote: We expect our Cluster 1 B200 1024 to go live somewhere in the mid-May, and in a couple of months, we are expecting to be able to deploy another cluster of 1024 which has already been planned.

items.statement: GPU demand strong both in India and globally; company prioritizes India first but fulfills global demand
items.quote: Yes, yes. There is fresh, we are seeing demand both in India as well as globally. It is strong both ways. We definitely try to prioritize India. But then wherever the demand comes from eventually, we are happy to fulfil it.

items.statement: No negative pricing pressure seen; spot rates for H100 up 25-30% in April; stability in pricing over extended periods with tailwinds inching prices up
items.quote: We do not see that there is any negative pressure on the pricing today. So, in fact, there are I think good set of tailwinds which are slowly inching up the prices rather than a decrease in pricing.

items.statement: March MRR reached INR374 million driven by utilization increase; government business (India AI Mission) not exceeding 35-40% of quarter revenue
items.quote: It is broadly an increase in overall utilization that has led to the increase in the spike in the March month. From the perspective of overall split, I think the India AI kind of -- Yes, so basically the overall government business across this quarter has not exceeded more than say 35%-40%.

items.statement: International revenue 35-37% of Q4; domestic 63-65%; no hard split on contract duration due to dynamic small base
items.quote: So, the international revenue for the last quarter is roughly around 35 odd percent. 35% to 37% is the international customer revenue.

items.statement: Overall infrastructure utilization ~80% in March (CPU, GPU, storage combined); excluding new B200s; elasticity to increase further
items.quote: Broadly across our entire infrastructure, not just GPUs, I think we are looking at like002080% plus utilization. Certainly across the quarter, I would say only in the March month, we are looking at 80% plus kind of utilization.

items.statement: FY27 capex not quantified; 2,048 B200s already planned; exploring private credit asset-light models for rapid GPU expansion beyond current plans
items.quote: Like we said we are already planning to deploy 2,048 B200. So that is already in place as far as our known plans are concerned. That being said, we are not limiting ourselves to those plans, so we continue to deploy capital under various business models judiciously to expand the GPU footprint fairly rapidly.

items.statement: Exploring private credit asset-light models alongside equity and debt to finance rapid GPU capacity expansion
